headline: THE FIRST PROPER COUNT OF THE CREATOR MARKET LANDED YESTERDAY AT 1.2 BILLION POUNDS, AND IT LEAVES OUT THE MONEY THAT MAKES CREATOR VIDEO WORK
deck: IAB UK published the first dedicated measurement of what brands pay creators.  It has the market growing at 26 percent while the rest of digital advertising grows at 9.6.  It also excludes paid amplification — the media money spent pushing a creator's post at people who do not follow that creator — and the practitioners it surveyed think amplification is two to three times the size of the fee.  So the number everybody will quote is roughly a quarter of what actually gets spent.
tldr: IAB UK's first measurement of the creator market puts UK partnership spend at 1.217 billion pounds for 2026, up 26 percent against 9.6 percent for the rest of digital, and explicitly excludes paid amplification that respondents estimate at two to three times the fee.  Pull your last three creator campaigns, add the creator fee to the media money spent pushing their posts, and recalculate your cost per result on the combined figure before your next budget conversation.

Google, Meta and Amazon took 56 percent of US ad revenue in 2025, up from 53 the year before, while machine-directed buying grew from 2 percent of the market in 2023 to about 12 in 2025 and is forecast at 27 percent by 2030.  Calculate what share of your budget was placed by a machine rather than chosen by a person, and set it next to what you spent on owned channels and direct creator relationships.

94 percent of TikTok Shop's US luxury resale revenue now comes from livestreams, with gross merchandise value up 400 percent year on year, because a live camera settles a condition question that a listing photograph cannot.  Write down the question your customers ask most before buying, and if a person pointing a camera could answer it in ten seconds, book a weekly live and let people ask it.

89 percent of European brands surveyed by Kolsquare expect to raise creator spend, 85 percent have expanded rosters and 37 percent now run more than 100 influencers, while the share connecting creator work to integrated brand campaigns fell from 45 percent to 32.  Name one person this week who owns creator work inside your campaign brief rather than beside it, and give them sign-off on the same brief everyone else runs from.

Dash Social reports that brands publishing six or fewer times a week get 20 percent higher engagement, that 55 percent of Instagram views come from non-followers, and that quarterly follower growth has fallen from 1.7 percent in 2023 to 0.9 in 2026 — though it publishes no sample size.  Cap next month's output at six posts a week and hand the recovered hours to the two ideas that were too odd to make at the old cadence.

The WARDOGS launch peaked at 452,600 concurrent viewers across platforms over four days against the Overwatch World Cup grand final's 401,000, with Twitch Drops running on nearly every channel and 1.6 billion of Twitch's 8.6 billion hours this year coming from Drops-enabled streams.  Demand peak, average, hours watched and airtime in one table on your next live buy, and ask outright whether a rewards mechanic was running in the quoted window.

Nicole Rudolph's median video is up 56.8 percent in five months to 208,363 views, and by our count her social history essays run about three times her house, personal and shopping-advice videos, with a straight fabric history beating the same question plus a buying guide by 3.2 to one.  If you sell fabric, clothing, footwear, tile, paint or fixtures, buy a read inside an essay she was already making rather than commissioning a video about your product.
